samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one corridor: a single connected staircase chain of equal square cells, one cell wide everywhere, that runs along, drops down by one cell, doubles back, drops again and runs along once more. Every pale grey mark lying outside that chain is inert decoration that means nothing. One end of the chain is capped by a solid black bar and the other end by a solid grey bar; both bars are walls. Each cell is tinted pale red, pale green, pale blue or pale yellow, and cells of the same tint always sit next to each other along the chain. In the upper half of every cell there is a floor pip: a solid black disc means step one cell away from the black bar, and a hollow black ring means step one cell towards the black bar. In the lower half of the cells there is exactly one red disc, the shover, and three solid brown squares, the crates. The floor pips are painted on the floor and never move. The replay goes like this, over and over: read the pip of the cell the shover is standing on and try to step one cell that way along the chain. If the next cell along is empty the shover moves into it. If the next cell along holds a crate, that crate is shoved one further cell the same way and the shover takes its place, but only if the cell beyond is inside the corridor and empty; otherwise nothing moves and the replay stops there. The replay also stops when the step would leave the corridor through either wall. The corridor may sit anywhere on the canvas. What is the tint of the cell the shover is resting on when the replay stops? Answer with one of red, green, blue or yellow.
